headline: High-risk filesystem and browser-enabled coding agent paired with offline image UI creates medium prompt/data/cascade risks, while direct capability conflict is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read workspace files and run browsers, so if ComfyUI outputs are manually copied into that workspace, prompt-like content could influence Cline. ComfyUI itself has no read_filesystem or clipboard surface, so there is no automatic bridge; the pathway is unusual and limited to manual transfer.
conditions: IF ComfyUI output is manually pasted or saved into Cline's workspace files
IF Cline is instructed to treat generated text from ComfyUI as instructions
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs in a separate folder not opened by Cline
Require a human review step before copying any generated text
Use a naming convention that marks generated artifacts as untrusted
Disable browser-driven ingestion of generated content where possible

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress, while ComfyUI is offline by default and does not read filesystems. The pair does not show a shared workspace or shared OAuth principal, so leakage is possible mainly through manual export of sensitive artifacts into Cline, not by default.
conditions: IF source code or screenshots are copied from Cline into ComfyUI workflows
IF Cline is configured to send workspace contents to external model providers
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in the Cline workspace
Use redacted screenshots for any shared artifacts
Confirm ComfyUI remains offline before exchanging files
Review Cline provider settings for outbound content handling

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the workspace filesystem and modify git state, but ComfyUI cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. Because ComfyUI lacks overlapping write authority, there is no same-resource write conflict; only limited coordination friction remains if both are pointed at the same human-managed assets.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same repository or asset directory
IF a human copies ComfyUI outputs into files Cline also edits
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs outside the git working tree
Use separate directories for generated media and code
Commit code changes before importing any generated assets
Avoid concurrent edits to the same folder

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can act on browser and filesystem outputs, so if ComfyUI-generated artifacts are treated as authoritative inputs, downstream mistakes can propagate into code or workflow changes. ComfyUI does not verify Cline's outputs, and no built-in cross-checking is shown, so the pair can form an unverified handoff in default human-mediated workflows.
conditions: IF Cline uses ComfyUI-generated artifacts as facts or specifications
IF a human forwards Cline's conclusions back into ComfyUI workflows without verification
mitigations: Require a human verification step before acting on generated artifacts
Separate generation from execution in different workspaces
Annotate ComfyUI outputs as non-authoritative
Use checklists for any code or workflow changes derived from generated media

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code and browser screenshots and may send content to a configured model provider, while ComfyUI is offline by default and touches media/model assets. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so the main compliance risk is limited to accidental movement of regulated content into Cline's outbound path.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Cline's workspace or screenshots
IF the configured model provider stores or processes that data outside required jurisdictions
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the Cline workspace
Use local or approved providers only
Strip identifiers from screenshots before use
Document a retention review for any exported artifacts
